title: Happening now
description: Say what you and others are doing right now, and what was going on at some time in the past.

guide.title: am / is / are doing: stem + -t- + the forms of iru
guide.text:
For an action in progress, Kannada joins the verb stem + t(aa) to the present forms of iru, 'to be': maadtaa iddeeni, literally 'doing I-am'. In normal speech this is pronounced and written as one word: ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ (maadtiddeeni).

Since you already know iddeeni, iddeeya, iddaane, iddaale, ide, you already know the endings.

Written forms: maaduttiddene (I), maaduttiddeeya (you), maaduttiddaane (he), maaduttiddaale (she), maaduttide (it).

Compare: naanu kelasa maadteeni, 'I work / I will work'; naanu kelasa maadtiddeeni, 'I am working (right now)'.

guide.title: Plural and respectful forms
guide.text:
The plural follows iru in the same way: -tiddeevi (we), -tiddeera (you, polite), -tiddaare (they / respectful), -tive (they, of things).

Written forms: maaduttiddeve, maaduttiddeeri, maaduttiddaare, maaduttive.

The stems are the same ones you learned for the present: hogtiddeeni (I am going), bartiddeeni (I am coming), nodtiddeeni (I am watching), odtiddeeni (I am reading). The -i and -e verbs keep their long vowel: kudeetiddeeni (I am drinking), kaleetiddeeni (I am learning). tinnu gives tintiddeeni (ತಿಂತಿದ್ದೀನಿ), 'I am eating'.

examples.english: They are doing. / He or she is doing. (respectful)

guide.title: Not doing, are you doing?, was doing
guide.text:
Negative: stem + -tilla, the same for every person: ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (maadtilla) 'am / is / are not doing'; bartilla, 'not coming'. Written: maaduttilla.

Question: add -aa as always. bartide - bartideyaa? 'is it coming?'; maadtiddeera - maadtiddeeraa? 'are you doing?'.

Was doing: replace the present of iru with its past (idde, idde, idda, idlu, ittu, idvi, idri, idru): ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೆ (maadtidde) I was doing; maadtidda, he was doing; maadtittu, it was doing; maadtidru, they were doing.

One trap: states that English expresses with '-ing' or an adjective are often a completed action in Kannada. 'He is sleeping / asleep' is malagiddaane, literally 'he has lain down'; 'she is sitting' is kootiddaale, 'she has sat'.

examples.english: He is asleep. (he has lain down)

phrases.note: A state: Kannada says 'has lain down', not 'is sleeping'.

phrases.english: She is talking on the phone.

phrases.note: Also said to mean 'I'm on my way'.

phrases.english: Where are you going? (to a friend)

phrases.note: -tilla is the same for all persons.
odu (long o) = to read, to study.
